definitions.gloss: hard of hearing; unable to hear well
definitions.explanation: Set phrase describing someone whose hearing has weakened, typically with age. Literally 'the ears are far'. It is the ordinary, unmarked way to say this in Japanese and is not itself impolite, though it is usually said of another person rather than to them.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}い。
examples.english: My grandmother is hard of hearing.

examples.japanese: {耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}い⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{話|はな}して→話す：00467_hanasu⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: I don't hear well, so please speak up.

examples.japanese: ⟦{年|とし}→年：00486_toshi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}って→取る：00565_toru⟧{耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}く⟦なって→なる：01970_naru⟧きた。
examples.english: My hearing has been going as I get older.

examples.japanese: ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}いふり⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{都合|つごう}→都合：01672_tsugou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}き{流|なが}す→聞き流す：07927_kikinagasu⟧。
examples.english: My father pretends to be hard of hearing and lets inconvenient topics pass right by.

notes:
The 〜⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{遠|とお}い→遠い：00529_tooi⟧ pattern treats a dulled sense as distance. It conjugates as an i-adjective phrase: {耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}く⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to grow hard of hearing), {耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}かった (was hard of hearing).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}く⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to start losing one's hearing
- ⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧{耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}い: to be a little hard of hearing
- {耳|みみ}が{遠|とお}いふり⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to pretend not to hear

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{耳|みみ}→耳：01513_mimi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{早|はや}い→早い：00514_hayai⟧: quick to hear news — same body-part idiom pattern, unrelated meaning
- ⟦{耳|みみ}が{痛|いた}い→耳が痛い：06892_mimigaitai⟧: it hurts to hear — used when criticism hits home
- ⟦{難聴|なんちょう}→難聴：18194_nanchou⟧: hearing loss — the clinical term used in medical contexts
